title: Rescale strategies for numeric coherence across kernels and KV cache
content:
Purpose
This is a working note on rescale strategies to keep numeric coherence when mixing precisions across: fused kernels, per-layer accumulators, and the KV cache. Goal: identify pragmatic rules and a small set of experiments to quantify failure modes (NaNs, blow-ups, silent drift).

Background / motivation
- We increasingly run models with hybrid FP16/FP8/INT8-like execution paths. Small differences in scaling make outputs diverge over time (esp for long context).
- KV cache stores cached keys/values that must be reused across requests; mismatched rescale semantics between forward pass and cache read lead to tiny biases that compound with autoregressive sampling.
- Observed failure modes: NaNs arising after a requantize step, large activation spikes at certain layers, and quality regressions on long-context prompts.

High-level hypotheses
1) Per-layer static scaling (single scale factor baked at quantization time) is brittle when kernels use fused accumulation vs elementwise accumulation.
2) Dynamic rescale on the accumulator (post-accumulate normalization) reduces overflow but introduces additional rounding that can change distribution and KV alignment relative to a fresh forward pass.
3) KV cache should store both the scaled tensor and a small scale metadata (exponent/scale-id) so reads can be re-normalized to the current runtime kernel's expected range.

Design candidates (brief)
A. Sticky-scale: attach a 16-bit scale descriptor to each KV block; on read, the kernel checks descriptor and rescales to runtime canonical FP range before using. Pros: minimal surprises; Cons: extra memory and per-read ops.
B. Canonical on-write rescale: whenever writing to KV cache, convert to a canonical internal range (float16-favoring exponent) using a fixed algorithm. Reads are direct. Pros: lower read cost; Cons: requires careful choice of canonical range that avoids overflow for all kernels/devices.
C. Accumulator post-rescale: perform accumulation in native higher precision (FP32 if available) and then downscale with stochastic rounding or deterministic rounding. Pros: safest numerical stability; Cons: performance hit on some devices, complexity with mixed-device fleets.
D. Layer-proximal scaling metadata: for each layer, maintain an epoch of scaling policy (e.g., 'A: bias-aware, B: clamp-to-max'); useful for rollouts and A/B compare.

Small experiment matrix (priority + quick win)
- E1 (quick): Add 8-bit scale-id metadata to KV rows and do a no-op rescale on read (float->float operation). Measure latency p95 increase and memory delta. Also run synthetic long-context sampling to check quality drift.
- E2: Implement canonical-on-write rescale + unit tests verifying round-trip (forward -> KV -> read -> forward) numerically equals a fresh forward within epsilon. Run eval set (100 prompts, 512->4096 sampling).
- E3: Compare stochastic vs deterministic rounding on accumulator downscale for FP8-path kernels. Metrics: NaN frequency, cosine similarity of logits, and sampling divergence.
- E4: Stress test multi-GPU hetero cluster: some workers run accumulator-in-FP32 and others FP16; assess cross-worker consistency for distributed KV sharding.

Microbench and observability plan
- Add counters: per-KV-block scale-id histogram, percent of reads that trigger rescale, per-layer rescale ops latency bucketed.
- E2/E3 require numeric delta histograms: per-token logit-diff distribution (mean/std), per-sequence BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxies.
- NaN/Inf poisoning detector: trace origin layer and scale metadata when the first NaN appears; store an example input + seed for reproduction.

Implementation details / pitfalls
- Metadata overhead: storing a float16-scale per 128 token block adds ~2 bytes * tokens/row; quantify for 4096 context. Consider scale-id table with global per-model scale entries referenced by 1-byte id to reduce memory.
- Rounding: stochastic rounding reduces bias but is non-deterministic. For debug/repro runs we need deterministic fallback. Provide a 'debug deterministic' flag.
- Kernel interfaces: prefer adding an optional 'scale_descriptor' arg to matmul/attention kernels instead of overloading existing buffers. This keeps API clear but requires rebuild across backends.
- Requantize placement: doing requantize after attention but before residual add reduces overflow cases but can make residual magnitude mismatch if different rescale policy used on the residual path. Ensure consistent rescale order across residual branches.

Preliminary observations (small-local runs)
- Using canonical-on-write reduced NaN incidents on a synthetic GPT2-like model when using aggressive FP8 modes (observed on A100 + older GPUs).
- Stochastic rounding cut down a small systematic drift but caused reproducibility issues in test harness; enabling deterministic RNG fixed this but reduced the benefit.
- Sticky-scale (metadata) approach was simplest to debug and allowed us to replay exact reads that caused NaNs. Latency overhead for small tests ~0.4% p95.

Open questions / risks
- How to handle cross-version model rollouts where older caches remain in KV across a rollout that changes canonical scaling? Need migration/compat strategy. Options: invalidate cache on rollout, or attach scale-version and rescale lazily on first read.
- Additional memory pressure from metadata at 4k contexts could be material for customer tiers that are memory-constrained. Is there a compression/quantized-id scheme acceptable?
- Dev/hardware heterogeneity: some customer private deployments may not support FP32 accumulators; must have a fallback policy.

Actionable next steps (concrete)
1) E1 prototype (sticky scale-id in KV) — 2 engineer-weeks: kernel change + cache format + unit tests + microbench.
2) Build NaN poisoning reproducibility harness (capture inputs/seeds/scale metadata) — 1 engineer-week.
3) Run E2 canonical-on-write on 3 model sizes (small/med/large) and evaluate sampling divergence → decide rollout default for hosted.
4) Draft migration policy: lazy-rescale on read + TTL for scale-versions; review with product for Dedicated/Private compatibility.

Notes to self / friction items
- Talk to infra: how does our on-disk KV persistence (if enabled) interact with new metadata? Might need a format bump and backwards compatibility layers.
- Coordinate with solutions-eng: some customers reported long-context hallucination drift; share early results to check correlation with our scaling experiments.
- Add a flag in runtime config to force deterministic rounding for debugging flakiness in CI.

References / reading
- internal PR: runtime#812 (KV-format prototype)
- papers: "On the Numeric Stability of Deep Learning Kernels" (internal summary), plus FP8 vendor notes

Appendix: quick checklist for experiment runs
- Ensure same random seeds + deterministic sampling toggles when comparing rounding modes.
- Collect per-layer scale histograms and store alongside run outputs.
- When NaN occurs: capture seed, input tokens, KV scale-id table snapshot, device type, and kernel build hash.

End of note — comments welcome.
